rows.verbatim_text: Conduct a thorough assessment of the patient including vital signs and physical exam in accordance with relevant patient care protocols.

Assess right to refuse/consent: • Patient must be at least 14 years of age to consent to or refuse care / transport. • Patient must not be subject to a court decree of incapacity or incompetence pertaining to healthcare decisions to refuse otherwise indicated care/transport.

Assess clinical decision-making capacity: • Ensure the patient is fully oriented (person, place, time, events) • Ensure the patient does not pose a foreseeable risk of harm to self or others • Ensure the patient understands the current clinical situation and proposed plan for treatment and/or transport, as well as any reasonable alternatives. • Ensure the patient understands the potential risks and benefits of accepting or refusing the proposed plan and any reasonable alternatives. • Ensure the patient is not under undue external influence. Consider discussion in private. • Assess for and take into consideration any condition which may impair decision making capacity such as acute or chronic psychiatric illness, acute drug or alcohol intoxication, CVA, hypotension, hypoglycemia, hypoxia, head trauma, or any other condition with similar effect. If a patient cannot express his/her wishes, either verbally or non-verbally, and no surrogate decision maker is available (see below), treatment should follow standard protocols.

Only if the patient is determined to lack capacity or competence, the following individuals may act as a surrogate decision maker, in descending order of authority: • Legal agent, guardian, or committee (appointed by a court of law) • Medical power of attorney (appointed by the patient) • Patient’s spouse – except in cases where divorce has been filed. • Adult child of the patient • Parent of the patient • Adult sibling of the patient • Other adult relative of the patient in descending order of blood relationship. Ensure the surrogate decision maker has clinical decision-making capacity (see above)

Clearly document the information provided to the patient/surrogate decision maker regarding potential risks and benefits of any proposed treatment and alternatives. If treatment and/or transport are refused, obtain signatures from the patient or authorized surrogate decision maker and at least one adult witness, when possible.

For patients in cardiac arrest: • DNR/DDNR/DNAR (Do Not Resuscitate) is applicable ONLY if the patient is in cardiac arrest. • Order such as POST, POLST, and MOLST forms may or may not include a specific DNR/DNI

order and are valid if signed by a physician. • valid DNR (original or unaltered physical or electronic copy issued in any state) or alternative DDNR jewelry is required to withhold resuscitation of patients not within

• valid living will or other advanced directive may be used to guide therapy and discussions

with surrogate decision makers/Medical Control, but is generally applicable only to terminal illness and should not be used to withhold attempts at resuscitation in the event of cardiac arrest. • DNR can be revoked at any time by the patient or authorized decision maker (if the decision maker initiated the DNR) by physically destroying the DNR order form or oral expression of intent to revoke. If there is any doubt as to the applicability or validity of a DNR or other advanced directive belonging
to a patient in cardiac arrest, begin CPR and contact Medical Control immediately for guidance.

For patients with acute psychiatric emergencies who present a significant risk of harm to themselves or others and are refusing treatment or transport, contact law enforcement regarding issuance of an Emergency Custody Order (ECO) for psychiatric evaluation.

For patients with acute medical emergencies who lack decision-making capacity or competence and are refusing treatment or transport, contact Medical Control regarding issuance of an Emergency Custody Order (ECO) for medical evaluation. Whenever possible, allow the Medical Control physician to speak directly with the patient or surrogate decision maker.

rows.verbatim_text: Follow Universal Patient Care / Initial Patient Contact protocol.

Scene Safety / PPE / Patient Contact • Utilize appropriate agencies and resources as needed to ensure patient and provider safety including lift assistance, personnel, ALS, or law enforcement. • Bring all necessary equipment to the patient’s side.

Initial Assessment • Perform Primary and Secondary Survey as indicated by patient status. • Consider spinal motion restriction if indicated by mechanism of injury or history from patient or witness. Refer to Spinal Motion Restriction procedure.

Ensure Adequate Airway, Oxygenation, and Ventilation • Manage airway by the least invasive means necessary. • Home oxygen should be maintained unless the patient’s oxygen saturation and/or symptoms indicate need for it to be increased. • Administer up to 15 LPM oxygen through an appropriate delivery device for the patient’s condition. • Refer to Airway Management and Ventilatory support procedure.

Vital Signs • Obtain blood pressure, pulse rate, respirations, and Glasgow Coma Scale. • Consider obtaining blood glucose level and temperature. • Closely monitor the patient, paying specific attention to their condition immediately before or after an intervention. o Stable: Reassess vital signs at least every 15 minutes o Unstable: Reassess vital signs at least every 5 minutes
Refer to relevant and appropriate protocols. If no protocol applies, or for clinical guidance at any time, consider contacting Medical Control.
Assess SpO2. Consider assessing EtCO2 and/or SpCO as indicated.
Consider 12-Lead ECG. Refer to Chest Pain (Cardiac) protocol. • Acquire within 5 minutes of patient contact. • Transmit to receiving facility within 10 minutes of patient contact.

Medication Administration • Confirm all medication administration “Rights”: o Right patient o Right medication o Right dose o Right route o Right time • Ensure medications are not expired. • Assess for drug-drug interactions and contraindications. o Refer to Pharmacology section and/or agency approved standard reference.
Establish IV / IO access when indicated. Refer to Intraosseous (IO) Access procedure, as needed.
Consider continuous cardiac monitoring.

Transport • Transport decisions should be based on patient’s clinical condition. Refer to relevant regional Field Triage policies regarding transport to specialty centers (Stroke, STEMI, Trauma). • Deliver a pre-arrival report to the receiving facility as soon as practical. • Consult with Medical Control regarding most appropriate destination or for clinical guidance whenever necessary. • Refer to Patient Refusal of Treatment / Transport policy, as needed.

If Fentanyl is not sufficient, administer: ADULT: Midazolam (Versed) 2.5 mg IV/IO over 2 minutes or 5 mg IN/IM PEDIATRIC: Midazolam (Versed) 0.1 mg/kg IV/IO over 2 minutes or 0.2 mg/kg IN/IM Maximum dose 2.5 mg IV/IO or 5 mg IN/IM Repeat every 10 - 15 minutes as needed for patient safety and comfort.

For cardiac arrest in renal dialysis patients, patients with crush injuries, suspected calcium channel blocker overdose, or suspected hyperkalemia only, also administer: ADULT: Calcium Chloride 1 g IV/IO slow push Followed by 20 mL 0.9% sodium chloride flush ADULT: Sodium Bicarbonate 50 mEq IV/IO slow push PEDIATRIC: Calcium Chloride 20mg/kg (max dose 1g) IV/IO slow push Followed by 20 mL 0.9% sodium chloride flush PEDIATRIC: Sodium Bicarbonate 1 mEq/kg (max dose 50 mEq) IV/IO slow push Repeat in 5 minutes if no change.

Obtain IV/IO access (humeral IO preferred if IV unavailable).
Consider: ADULT: 0.9% Sodium chloride up to 1 L IV/IO in 250 – 500 mL boluses PEDIATRIC: 0.9% Sodium chloride 20 mL/kg IV/IO Repeat as needed to maintain adequate perfusion, up to 60 mL/kg total.

Maintain mean arterial pressure (MAP) above 65 mmHg. Consider: ADULT: Norepinephrine (Levophed) infusion 5 – 20 mcg/min IV/IO (Add 4 mg of Norepinephrine to 250 mL 0.9% Sodium chloride = 16 mcg/mL) OR ADULT: Epinephrine infusion 2 – 10 mcg/min IV/IO (Add 1 mg of Epinephrine [1mg/mL] to 100 mL of 0.9% Sodium chloride = 10 mcg/mL)

Maintain age adjusted SBP. Consider: PEDIATRIC: Epinephrine 0.1 - 1 mcg/kg/min IV/IO infusion. Max dose: 10 mcg/min. Under 1 year old: Titrate to SBP > 70 mmHg Over 1 year old: Titrate to SBP > 90 mmHg (Add 1 mg of Epinephrine [1mg/mL] to 100 mL of 0.9% Sodium chloride = 10 mcg/mL) Note: Infusion via IV pump is preferred is available. Monitor closely for signs of extravasation.

To maintain MAP > 65 until a vasopressor infusion is prepared, consider: ADULT: Push dose Epinephrine 5-10 mcg IV/IO every 2-3 minutes (Add 100 mcg Epinephrine (1mL of 0.1 mg/mL) to 9mL of 0.9% Normal Saline = 10 mcg / mL)

Open the airway. Refer to Airway Management and Ventilatory Support procedure.

Apply AED or cardiac monitor. Assess rhythm (I / P): For Asystole at the time of EMS arrival: Consider withholding / terminating resuscitation. For PEA/Witnessed Asystole: Continue CPR. For VF/VT: Continue CPR and defibrillate.

Obtain IV/IO access. Establish secondary IV/IO access if possible. If blood products are not available, administer: ADULT: 0.9% Sodium chloride up to 1 L IV/IO in 250 – 500 mL boluses PEDIATRIC: 0.9% Sodium chloride 20 mL/kg IV/IO Repeat as needed to maintain adequate perfusion, up to 60 mL/kg total.

If signs or suspicion of thoracoabdominal trauma are present (blunt or penetrating), perform bilateral chest decompression. Follow Chest Decompression procedure. Note: CPR should NOT impede procedural interventions when treating traumatic cardiac arrest.*
If ROSC is not achieved, and rhythm remains PEA, administer: ADULT: 1 mg Epinephrine 0.1 mg/mL IV/IO PEDIATRIC: 0.01 mg/kg Epinephrine IV/IO Single dose only.

If there are no signs of life after 15-20 minutes of resuscitation, or at any time for additional guidance including optimal destination determination, contact Medical Control. If transporting and the patient is in cardiac arrest, transport to the closest Emergency Department.
Follow Universal Patient Care / Initial Patient Contact protocol.
Determine DNR status. Refer to Death and Criteria for Withholding Resuscitation protocol.
Begin chest compression. Follow Adult/Pediatric Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) procedure.
Identify and treat potentially reversible causes. See Pearls below.

Administer: ADULT: 0.9% Sodium Chloride IV/IO up to 1 L in 250 – 500 mL boluses PEDIATRIC: 0.9% Sodium Chloride 20 mL/kg IV/IO Repeat as needed to maintain adequate perfusion, up to 60 mL/kg total.

If VF or VT is present, or AED is advising to shock [EMR], immediately defibrillate: ADULT: 200 joules Biphasic / 360 joules Monophasic, or manufacturer’s recommendation. PEDIATRIC: 2 joules/kg initial, 4 joules/kg subsequent After each defibrillation, perform 2 minutes of CPR, followed by rhythm assessment. If VF / VT persists, defibrillate again, then consider medication therapy as listed below.
Administer: ADULT: Epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO [0.1 mg/mL concentration] PEDIATRIC: Epinephrine 0.01 mg/kg IV/IO [0.1 mg/mL concentration] Repeat every 3-5 minutes during cardiac arrest.

If apneic/bradypneic, provide respiratory support and administer: ADULT: Naloxone (Narcan) 1 – 2 mg IN PEDIATRIC: Naloxone (Narcan) 1 -2 mg IN Repeat at double the initial dose if no response in 5 minutes.

If apneic/bradypneic, provide respiratory support and administer: ADULT: Naloxone (Narcan) 0.5 – 2 mg IV/IO slow push or IM/IN PEDIATRIC: Naloxone (Narcan) 0.1 mg/kg IV/IO slow push or IM/IN. Maximum dose 2 mg. Repeat at double the initial dose if no response in 5 minutes.

If hypotensive with signs of poor perfusion, administer: ADULT: Calcium chloride 1 g IV/IO slow push Followed by a 20 mL 0.9% sodium chloride flush PEDIATRIC: Calcium Chloride 20mg/kg (max dose 1g) IV/IO slow push Followed by 20 mL 0.9% sodium chloride flush AND ADULT: Glucagon 1 mg IV/IO slow push PEDIATRIC (< 25 kg): Glucagon 0.5 mg IV/IO slow push PEDIATRIC (≥ 25 kg): Glucagon 1 mg IV/IO slow push If no response, refer to Hypotension and Shock protocol.

For respiratory distress due to bronchorrhea, administer: ADULT: Atropine sulfate 2 mg IV/IO/IM PEDIATRIC (< 40 kg): Atroprine sulfate 1mg IV/IO/IM PEDIATRIC (≥ 40 kg): Atropine sulfate 2 mg IV/IO/IM Repeat every 5 minutes until respiratory secretions reduce and work of breathing improves.

Anti-Cholinergic & Tricyclic Antidepressant (TCA) Begin active cooling if temperature is greater than 104F / 40C. Refer to Heat stroke / Hyperthermia protocol. Assess and monitor cardiac rhythm. For wide QRS (Adult: > 120 ms, Ped: > 90 ms) or arrhythmia,

administer: ADULT: Sodium bicarbonate 50 mEq IV/IO slow push PEDIATRIC: Sodium bicarbonate 1 mEq/kg IV/IO slow push. Maximum dose 50 mEq. Repeat once in 5 – 10 minutes for cardiac arrest or persistent ECG changes.

For altered mental status, seizures, hypotension, and/or cardiac arrest following exposure to combustion products in an enclosed space or suspected cyanide poisoning, administer (if available): ADULT: Hydroxocobalamin (CYANOKIT) 5 g IV/IO, infuse over 15 minutes PEDIATRIC: Hydroxocobalamin (CYANOKIT) 70 mg/kg IV/IO, infuse over 15 minutes To reconstitute for infusion: Add: 200mL of 0.9% Sodium Chloride to Hydroxocobalamin (CYANOKIT) vial using the transfer spike included in the kit. Fill to the line. Mix: Repeatedly invert or rock the vial for at least 60 seconds. Do not shake.
Contact Medical Control for guidance as needed.
Follow Universal Patient Care / Initial Patient Contact protocol.
Perform a focused evaluation including pertinent history and assessment of airway and lung sounds. Refer to Airway Management and Ventilatory Support procedure (includes airway foreign body).
Provide supplemental oxygen to maintain SpO2 > 94%.
Consider non-invasive (CPAP) or invasive (SGA) ventilatory support.

Consider invasive ventilatory support via endotracheal intubation. Refer to Endotracheal Intubation procedure. Note: Intubation of spontaneously breathing patients without rapid sequence induction (RSI) is generally not recommended. RSI is not addressed in PEMS regional protocols – refer to agency specific protocols for guidance.

Administer: ADULT: Albuterol Sulfate 3 mL of 0.083% solution, nebulized. Repeat as necessary. ADULT: Ipratropium Bromide 3 mL of 0.02% solution, nebulized. Once. PEDIATRIC: Albuterol Sulfate 3 mL of 0.083% solution, nebulized. Repeat as necessary. PEDIATRIC: Ipratropium Bromide 3 mL of 0.02% solution, nebulized. Once.

For moderate to severe symptoms, also administer: ADULT: Methylprednisolone (Solu-Medrol) 125 mg IV/IO slow push. PEDIATRIC: Methylprednisolone (Solu-Medrol) 2 mg/kg IV/IO slow push. Maximum dose: 125 mg
For severe symptoms, also administer: ADULT: Magnesium Sulfate 2 g IV/IO infusion over 15 minutes PEDIATRIC: Magnesium Sulfate 40 mg/kg IV/IO over 15 minutes. Maximum dose: 2,000 mg (2 g)
Administer: ADULT: Epinephrine 3 mg [1 mg/mL] nebulized PEDIATRIC: Epinephrine 3 mg [1 mg/mL] nebulized May repeat once, if needed.

For moderate to severe symptoms, also administer: ADULT: Methylprednisolone (Solu-Medrol) 125 mg IV/IO slow push. PEDIATRIC: Methylprednisolone (Solu-Medrol) 2 mg/kg IV/IO slow push. Maximum dose: 125 mg
Provide suctioning as needed and consider: PEDIATRIC: 0.9% Sodium Chloride, 6 mL nebulized. Repeat as needed for increased work of breathing due to secretions.
Administer: ADULT: Nitroglycerine 0.4 mg SL If SBP remains greater than 100 mmHg (MAP 65 mmHg), may repeat every five minutes as needed, up to three doses.
Administer: ADULT: Furosemide (Lasix) 40 mg IV/IO slow push
Contact Medical Control for guidance as needed.
Follow Universal Patient Care / Initial Patient Contact protocol.
Prevent the patient from sustaining injury, but do not restrain while actively seizing.
Provide supplemental oxygen. Refer to Airway Management and Ventilatory Support procedure.
Refer to Overdose / Poisoning / Toxic Ingestion protocol, as needed.
Assess blood glucose level. Refer to Hypoglycemia / Hyperglycemia protocol, as needed.

If actively seizing for over 5 minutes, administer: ADULT: Midazolam (Versed) 5 mg IV/IO or 10 mg IM PEDIATRIC (< 40 kg): Midazolam (Versed) 2.5 mg IV/IO or 5 mg IM PEDIATRIC (> 40 kg): Midazolam (Versed) 5 mg IV/IO or 10 mg IM Repeat the initial dose once in 5 minutes if seizure activity continues. Use half dose Midazolam for frail, hypotensive, underweight, and/or elderly ( > 65 years) patients.

If seizure activity continues for more than 5 minutes following administration of the second dose of Midazolam, initiate transport to the closest emergency department and contact medical control for guidance.
Follow Universal Patient Care / Initial Patient Contact protocol.

Obtain IV/IO access. Administer:* ADULT: 0.9% Sodium chloride up to 1 L IV/IO in 250 – 500 mL boluses PEDIATRIC: 0.9% Sodium chloride 20 mL/kg IV/IO Repeat as needed to maintain adequate perfusion, up to 60 mL/kg total.

Maintain mean arterial pressure (MAP) above 65 mmHg. Consider: ADULT: Norepinephrine (Levophed) infusion 5 – 20 mcg/min IV/IO (Add 4 mg of Norepinephrine to 250 mL 0.9% Sodium chloride = 16 mcg/mL) OR ADULT: Epinephrine infusion 2 – 10 mcg/min IV/IO (Add 1 mg of Epinephrine [1mg/mL] to 100 mL of 0.9% Sodium chloride = 10 mcg/mL)

Maintain age adjusted SBP. Consider: PEDIATRIC: Epinephrine 0.1 - 1 mcg/kg/min IV/IO infusion. Max dose: 10 mcg/min. Under 1 year old: Titrate to SBP > 70 mmHg Over 1 year old: Titrate to SBP > 90 mmHg (Add 1 mg of Epinephrine [1mg/mL] to 100 mL of 0.9% Sodium chloride = 10 mcg/mL) Note: Infusion via IV pump is preferred is available. Monitor closely for signs of extravasation.

To maintain MAP > 65 mmHg until a vasopressor infusion is prepared, consider: ADULT: Push dose Epinephrine 5-10 mcg IV/IO every 2-3 minutes (Add 100 mcg Epinephrine (1mL of 0.1 mg/mL) to 9mL of 0.9% Normal Saline = 10 mcg / mL)
Contact Medical Control for guidance as needed, and advise of a “Prehospital Sepsis Alert.”
Follow Universal Patient Care / Initial Patient Contact protocol.
Assess probability of large vessel occlusion (LVO) using RACE stroke scale. See table below.
Record time the patient last seen normal and family contact information, if available.* Provide this information to the receiving facility.
Obtain blood glucose level. If less than 60 mg/dL, refer to Hypoglycemia protocol.

Initiate transport. Goal scene time < 15 minutes: Symptoms less than 24 hours (or unknown) AND suspected LVO (RACE = 5 - 9) : Transport to the closest comprehensive stroke center as long as transport time is not increased by greater than 30 minutes. Symptoms greater than 24 hours OR low suspicion for LVO (RACE = 0 - 4): Transport to the closest stroke center.
Contact Medical Control for guidance as needed.
Follow Universal Patient Care / Initial Patient Contact protocol.
Obtain and transmit a 12-Lead ECG.

Obtain IV access. Consider: ADULT: 0.9% Sodium chloride up to 1 L IV/IO in 250 – 500 mL boluses PEDIATRIC: 0.9% Sodium chloride 20 mL/kg IV/IO Repeat as needed to maintain adequate perfusion, up to 60 mL/kg total.

If the rhythm is regular, consider: ADULT: Adenosine (Adenocard) 6 mg IV/IO followed by a 20 mL 0.9% Sodium chloride flush. PEDIATRIC: Adenosine (Adenocard) 0.1 mg/kg IV/IO followed by a 10 – 20 mL 0.9% Sodium chloride flush. Maximum dose 6 mg. If no conversion within 2 minutes, consider repeating one time at double the initial dose.
If the rhythm is irregular/atrial fibrillation, initiate transport to an appropriate facility. Monitor for signs of poor perfusion.

For light sedation, if time and patient condition permit, consider: ADULT: Midazolam (Versed) 2.5 mg IV/IO or 5 mg IN/IM PEDIATRIC: Midazolam (Versed) 0.05 mg/kg IV/IO or 0.1 mg/kg IM. Maximum dose 2.5 mg IV/IO or 5 mg IM. Monitor SpO2 and EtCO2.

Perform synchronized cardioversion. ADULT: 100 joules initial dose If cardioversion is unsuccessful, check pad placement and repeat at 200 joules. PEDIATRIC: 1 joule/kg initial dose If cardioversion is unsuccessful, check pad placement and repeat at 2 joules/kg. If cardioversion is unsuccessful after two attempts, contact Medical Control for guidance.
Contact Medical Control if uncertain regarding rhythm, most appropriate therapy, and for guidance as needed. Ensure a 12-Lead ECG is transmitted.

PEDIATRIC: Contact Medical Control for guidance. If no conversion within 2 minutes, consider repeating one time at double the initial dose.

If cardioversion is unsuccessful after two attempts, contact Medical Control for guidance.

PEDIATRIC: 1 joules/kg initial dose If cardioversion is unsuccessful, check pad placement and repeat at 2 joules/kg.

rows.section_heading: Unstable Ventricular Tachycardia with a Pulse
rows.verbatim_text: Contact Medical Control if uncertain regarding rhythm, most appropriate therapy, and for guidance as needed. Ensure a 12-Lead ECG is transmitted.
Follow Universal Patient Care / Initial Patient Contact protocol. Don appropriate PPE including gloves (sterile if available), gown, and eye protection.
Remove all clothing below the waist. Visualize perineum and assess for crowning or presenting part.
If significant bleeding, refer to Hemorrhagic Shock protocol.
If breech presentation or cord prolapse, refer to guidance below.
If crowning, apply gentle pressure on the bony part of the skull (not fontanel) for controlled delivery.
Once head is delivered, assess for nuchal cord. Unwrap if possible. Clamp and cut if necessary.

Support the head while delivering the shoulders and torso. Shoulder Dystocia If unable to deliver the anterior shoulder, place the patient in McRobert’s position (see image below) and apply suprapubic pressure. If no progress, contact Medical Control immediately for guidance.
Once delivery is complete, dry and stimulate the neonate. Assess heart rate, respirations, and oxygen saturation. Follow Neonatal Resuscitation protocol.
Routine suctioning is no longer recommended. Only perform pharyngeal/tracheal suctioning if thick

meconium is present or when the airway is obstructed. If the neonate does not require immediate resuscitation, consider delayed cord clamping until 1 – 3 minutes after birth. When pulsation of the cord has ceased, place clamps at approximately 4” and 6” from the neonate. Cut between them. Keep the baby warm and monitor closely. Assess for additional pregnancies. If none, apply gentle traction to the umbilical cord and perform
fundal massage until the placenta delivers and bleeding stops. Transport the placenta with the mother.

If possible, allow skin to skin contact for the mother and baby. Apply direct pressure to any visible sites of bleeding. If bleeding continues, refer to Hemorrhagic Shock protocol and initiate transport, preferably to a facility with Obstetric capability if condition allows. PEMS Regional Patient Care Protocols, Policies and Procedures

orphans.text: • Rupture of membranes (loss of fluid) prior to 37 weeks gestation is considered premature. These patients are at an increased risk of umbilical cord prolapse and need for resuscitation of the neonate. • Hypotension not associated with blood loss should be addressed with IV fluids and, if possible, relieving weight on the IVC by placing the patient in a left lateral recumbent position. • Consider

rows.verbatim_text: Follow Universal Patient Care / Initial Patient Contact protocol.
Transport to a facility with labor and delivery capability.
If actively seizing or a seizure has occurred (Eclampsia), administer: ADULT: Magnesium Sulfate 4 g IV/IO infusion over 10 minutes.
If seizure continues for more than five minutes, also administer: ADULT: Midazolam (Versed) 5 mg IV/IO or 10 mg IM Use half dose Midazolam for frail, hypotensive, and/or underweight patients.
If seizures continue or reoccur, contact medical control for guidance including transport destination.
Follow General – Universal Patient Care/Initial Patient Contact protocol.
Support life threatening problems associated with airway, breathing and circulation.
Administer oxygen as needed per patient assessment.
Place patient in left lateral recumbent position and transport immediately.
Establish IV access and administer 20 mL/kg 0.9% Normal Saline bolus up to A 1,000 mL; continuously reassessing need for further fluid administration.
Follow Universal Patient Care / Initial Patient Contact protocol.
Consider gross decontamination.
Follow Airway Management and Ventilatory Support procedure.
Administer: ADULT: Albuterol Sulfate 3 mL of 0.083% solution, nebulized. Repeat as necessary.

PEDIATRIC: Albuterol Sulfate 3 mL of 0.083% solution, nebulized. Repeat as necessary. Administer: ADULT: Methylprednisolone (Solu-Medrol) 125 mg IV/IO slow push. PEDIATRIC: Methylprednisolone (Solu-Medrol) 2 mg/kg IV/IO slow push. Maximum dose: 125 mg For suspected Chlorine gas exposure, consider: ADULT: Sodium bicarbonate 2 mL diluted with 2 mL 0.9% Sodium chloride, nebulized. Once. PEDIATRIC: Sodium bicarbonate 2 mL diluted with 2 mL 0.9% Sodium chloride, nebulized. Once.
Contact Medical Control for guidance as needed.
Follow Universal Patient Care / Initial Patient Contact protocol.
Consider gross decontamination.
Follow Airway Management and Ventilatory Support procedure.
Refer to Sepsis protocol, as needed.
Contact Medical Control for guidance as needed.
Follow Universal Patient Care / Initial Patient Contact protocol.
Consider gross decontamination. Remove clothing and copiously irrigate exposed areas.
Follow Airway Management and Ventilatory Support procedure. Refer to Respiratory Distress protocol, as needed.
If chemical burns are present, follow Burn Injuries protocol.
Contact Medical Control for guidance as needed.
Follow Universal Patient Care / Initial Patient Contact protocol.
Don appropriate PPE and decontaminate the patient. Do not proceed until it is reasonably safe to do so.
Follow Airway Management and Ventilatory Support procedure.
Refer to Nausea / Vomiting, Seizure, and/or Hypotension and Shock protocols, as needed.
If available, administer: ADULT: DuoDote Autoinjector IM PEDIATRIC (≥ 40 kg): DuoDote Autoinjector IM If symptoms persist, repeat in 5 minutes up to three doses.

If symptoms persist, or if DuoDote Autoinjector is unavailable, administer: ADULT: Atropine sulfate 2 mg IV/IO/IM PEDIATRIC (< 40 kg): Atropine sulfate 1 mg IV/IO/IM PEDIATRIC (≥ 40 kg): Atropine sulfate 2 mg IV/IO/IM If symptoms persist, repeat every 5 minutes up to three doses.
Contact Medical Control for guidance as needed.
Follow Universal Patient Care / Initial Patient Contact protocol.
Follow Airway Management and Ventilatory Support protocol.
If there is a life-threatening illness or injury, treat the patient without regard for contamination.*
If there is no life-threatening condition, determine if the patient is contaminated. See Pearls below.
Consider gross decontamination.
Contact Medical Control for guidance as needed.
Prepare and power on the cardiac monitor, connect 12-Lead cables, and attach electrodes.
Apply extremity leads:  RA (white) to right arm  LA (red) to left arm  RL (green) to right leg  LL (black) to left leg

Expose the chest and apply precordial leads (see image below):  V1 to 4 th intercostal space at right sternal border  V2 to 4 th intercostal space at left sternal border  V3 midway between V2 and V4  V4 to 5 th intercostal space at left midclavicular line  V5 level with V4 at left anterior axillary line  V6 level with V5 at left midaxillary line
Input the patient’s age and sex, instruct the patient to remain still, and acquire the ECG.

If no EMT-I or Paramedic is available to assess the ECG, or if it is interpreted by an EMT-I or Paramedic to represent an acute cardiac emergency (e.g. acute dysrhythmia), transmit the ECG to the most appropriate facility and notify Medical Control that an ECG has been transmitted.

If the 12-Lead ECG reads “STEMI” or “ACUTE MI,” transmit the ECG to the closest PCI capable hospital. Notify the receiving facility of a “Pre-Hospital STEMI Alert.” Follow Chest Pain (Cardiac) protocol.

Provide a copy (printed or electronic) of the ECG(s) to the receiving facility or HEMS crew. Ensure patient name, DOB, and time acquired are provided on the printed ECG. Attach a digital copy of the ECG to the patient care report.

If the 12-Lead ECG is atypical or indeterminate, there is high suspicion for cardiac ischemia, or there is concern for an acute cardiac emergency, transmit the ECG to the most appropriate facility and contact Medical Control for guidance.
Follow General – Universal Patient Care / Initial Patient Contact protocol.
Determine DNR status. Refer to Death & Criteria for Withholding Resuscitation protocol.

Begin chest compressions. Push hard and fast. Allow full chest recoil. Limit pauses to <10 sec. Depth: At least 2 inches deep Rate: 100 – 120 bpm Adult: Finger interlocked, mid-chest on the sternum Administer 100% oxygen. Do not over-ventilate.
Maintain compression-ventilation ratio 30:2 until advanced airway is established, then administer one breath every six seconds.

If respiratory pathogen is suspected, consider early intubation and HEPA filtered ventilation (I/P only). Apply AED / Assess cardiac rhythm every 2 minutes. If AED is advising to shock or rhythm is VF or VT (as determined by EMT-I or P) defibrillate at maximum joules, then refer to Cardiac Arrest: Ventricular Fibrillation / Pulseless Ventricular Tachycardia protocol. If AED is advising no shock or rhythm is asystole or PEA (as determined by EMT-I or P), continue CPR then refer to Cardiac Arrest: Asystole / Pulseless Electrical Activity protocol. Alternate compressors every 2 minutes or sooner if fatigued.
Consider mechanical CPR device, if available.
Monitor ETCO2. If ETCO2 < 10 or dropping, reassess and optimize compression rate, depth, and recoil.
If ROSC is achieved, refer to Post Cardiac Arrest Care (ROSC) protocol.
If ROSC is not achieved, refer to Death and Criteria for Withholding Resuscitation protocol. Note: Once initiated, termination of resuscitative efforts is a Medical Control decision only.
Follow Universal Patient Care / Initial Patient Contact protocol.
Refer to appropriate protocol (e.g. Respiratory Distress) for condition specific therapy guidelines.
Provide suctioning as needed to maintain patent airway.

Foreign body airway obstruction: * ADULT: Perform Heimlich abdominal thrusts. OBESE / PREGNANT: Perform chest thrusts. PEDIATRIC ≥ 1 year: Perform Heimlich abdominal thrusts. PEDIATRIC < 1 year: Alternate 5 back blows/chest thrusts until obstruction clears
Provide / titrate supplemental oxygen via NC or NRB to maintain SpO 94 – 98%. 2 Use EtCO2 monitor to guide therapy. Refer to Capnography procedure.
Consider CPAP (PEEP: 5 cmH2O) for respiratory distress. Refer to CPAP procedure. I/P only: Adjust PEEP to support ventilation and work of breathing, up to 10 cmH O.** 2
Position the patient and open the airway. Use BLS airway adjuncts (OPA/NPA/SGA) as necessary.
Support respirations with BVM. Use in-line EtCO2. Refer to Capnography procedure. Adjust tidal volume, respiratory rate, and/or PEEP (if available) to maintain EtCO 35 – 45mmHg.** 2
Foreign body airway obstruction: If unable to ventilate, perform laryngoscopy. Remove with forceps.
If apneic and ≥ 12 years old: Consider endotracheal intubation if unable to ventilate adequately by less invasive means. Follow Endotracheal Intubation procedure.
If apneic and < 12 years old: consider endotracheal intubation if unable to ventilate adequately by less invasive means. Follow Endotracheal Intubation procedure.****
Adequate respiratory effort: Apply ETCO2 sampling nasal cannula to patient.
Inadequate respiratory effort / Apnea: Attach inline ETCO2 sampling device to BVM, CPAP, or ventilator.
Continuously monitor reading and waveform. Refer to waveform guide below.

Advanced airway (ETT/SGA): Continuous monitoring ETCO2 waveform is required at all times. Any sudden drop or loss of ETCO2 signal must be addressed immediately, beginning with reverification of airway device placement and adequate ventilation.
Cardiac Arrest: If ETCO2 < 10 or dropping during CPR, optimize compression rate, depth, and recoil. If ROSC is achieved, adjust ventilation to maintain ETCO2 of 35-45 mmHg. Do not hyperventilate.
Head Injury / TBI / Stroke: Adjust ventilation to maintain ETCO2 of 35-45 mmHg. Do not hyperventilate.
Obstructive airway disease (Asthma / COPD): Consider permissive hypercapnia. Prioritize oxygenation.
Administer oxygen at 15 LPM (100% FiO2).

Locate the second intercostal space in the mid-clavicular line on the same side as the suspected pneumothorax. Cleanse the site. Alternate acceptable position: Fourth intercostal space, midaxillary line.

Attach a 10 mL syringe filled with 0.9% Sodium Chloride to a 14-gauge catheter needle – use longest available. Aspirate the syringe while advancing over the rib, perpendicular to the skin, and into the pleural space until a pop is felt or air/blood/fluid is freely aspirated. Do not advance the needle further.
Advance the catheter over the needle into the pleural space and remove the needle.
Reassess the patient, including vital signs and respiratory effort / compliance. Consider repeating the above steps for continued or recurrent hemodynamic instability.
Ensure adequate oxygen supply to the CPAP device. Explain the procedure and indications to the patient.
Set positive and expiratory pressure (PEEP) to 5 mmHg
Place the mask over the mouth and nose with oxygen flowing. Secure with straps, beginning with the lower straps. Tighten until air-leak is minimal.
Reassess the patient, including the SpO2, ETCO2, and work of breathing.
Consider titratingPEEP9%-15mmHg) as needed to improve ventilation/work of breathing. CPAP, BiPAP, and PEEP are RED DOT procedures at all EMS Certification Levels
Follow Universal Patient Care / Initial Patient Contact protocol.
Pre-oxygenate the patient: Provide 100% Oxygen via NRB or BVM for 3 minutes. Monitor SpO2. Refer to Airway Management and Ventilatory Support protocol.
Position the patient: Ear to sternal notch.
Maintain in-line cervical spine stabilization if there is concern for trauma.

Prepare equipment: o IV/IO access o ET tube of appropriate size + 1 size below o Stylet or bougie o Oxygen ON o Suction ON o Laryngoscope o Back up airway (e.g. Supraglottic airway device) o BVM with ETCO2 monitor attached Orally intubate. Patients 12 years and older. Advance laryngoscope in the midline, identifying airway structures progressively. Ensure
tube and cuff are visualized passing through the vocal cords.
Orally Intubate. Patients < 12 years old.
If unsuccessful, reoxygenate between attempts with 100% Oxygen. Adjust positioning/technique/equipment as necessary prior to any further attempt.
After two failed attempts, airway must be managed by the most experienced provider available.
If unable to intubate and unable to oxygenate, proceed immediately to Surgical Airway.
Verify placement. o

Ensure the presence of continuous box-waveform capnography. o Auscultate for bilateral lung sounds & absence of gastric sounds Secure the tube. Use tape or commercial tube holder. Document the depth of placement. Administer analgesia/sedation, as needed for patient safety and comfort. Refer to
the Sedation Post Advanced Airway Protocol.
Monitor ET tube placement and ventilation with SpO2 and Continuous box waveform ETCO2

Locate an appropriate insertion site. Avoid insertion through infected tissue and into bone suspected to be fractured. Cleanse the site with an alcohol pad or disinfectant swab. • Proximal humerus: Internally rotate the arm and locate the greater tubercle approximately 2 finger breadths above the humeral neck. Approach from the side at a 45° angle. • Proximal tibia: 2-3 finger breaths below the Patella and 2 finger breadths medial along the flat aspect of the Tibia.
Insert the IO needle into the selected site with the needle perpendicular to the bone surface until the needle tip touches the bone. Confirm at least one black line on the needle is visible above the
skin. Penetrate the bone by squeezing the driver’s trigger and apply gentle, steady, downward pressure. Release the trigger when a loss of resistance is felt upon entry into the medullary space.
Stabilize the catheter hub and remove the driver from the needle. Remove the stylet by turning counterclockwise. Dispose of the stylet in an appropriate container for sharp biohazards.
Secure the needle and attach primed extension tubing to the Luer-lock. If the patient is unconscious, aspirate to confirm placement then flush with 10 – 20 mL 0.9% Sodium Chloride.

If the patient is conscious, administer: ADULT: 2% Lidocaine 1 mg/kg IO slow push. Maximum dose 40 mg. PEDIATRIC: 2% Lidocaine 0.5 mg/kg IO slow push. Maximum dose 20 mg. Allow Lidocaine to dwell for one minute, then flush with 0.9% sodium chloride. May repeat once, as necessary for pain control.
Once IO access is obtained and verified, refer to Medication Administration procedure.

Assess VAD. Look / Listen for alarms. Listen for VAD hum. If batteries are depleted, connect to alternate power source, or replace one battery at a time with the assistance of the patient, a trained family member, or the device coordinator. Do not remove both batteries at the same time.
Assess perfusion (skin color, skin temperature, capillary refill).
Assess cardiac rhythm. Follow protocols for arrhythmias. Cardiovert/defibrillate if indicated.
If hypotensive, perfusion is inadequate, or alarm reads “Low Flow,” contact the device coordinator and/or Medical Control for guidance prior to administering IVF or vasopressors.

rows.section_heading: VAD: Unconscious Patient, VAD Not Functioning
rows.verbatim_text: Attempt to restart VAD. Ensure driveline and power source are connected. Ensure batteries have charge. If still not restarted, replace system controller (See pearls).

rows.section_heading: VAD: Unconscious Patient, VAD Not Functioning
rows.verbatim_text: If unable to restart the device: Begin chest compressions. Reassess cardiac rhythm / apply AED, and follow appropriate Cardiac Arrest protocols. Defibrillate if indicated. Administer ACLS medications as indicated.
If perfusion is adequate, assess for alternate causes of altered mental status (e.g. hypoxia, hypoglycemia, overdose, stroke) and follow standard protocols.

If perfusion is inadequate, assess MAP and/or intubate and assess ETCO2**. If unable to intubate, SGA may be used.  ETCO2 above 20 mmHg or MAP above 50 mmHg: Assess for alternate causes of poor perfusion (e.g. sepsis, hypovolemia, allergic reaction).  ETCO2 below 20 mmHg or MAP below 50 mmHg: Begin chest compressions. Reassess cardiac rhythm and follow appropriate Cardiac Arrest protocols. Defibrillate if indicated. Administer ACLS medications as indicated.
For all other device issues contact the device coordinator and/or Medical Control for guidance.

If hypotensive or showing signs of inadequate perfusion, refer to Hypotension and Shock protocol. Contact device coordinator and/or Medical Control immediately for guidance. Do not administer vasopressors. Do not obtain ECG. Do not attempt pacing.

If unresponsive and without palpable pulses, assist ventilations. Ensure the drive line and power source are connected. Ensure batteries have charge and replace if necessary. Contact the device coordinator and/or Medical Control for guidance.

Do not begin chest compressions. Do not obtain ECG. Do not cardiovert/defibrillate. For all other device issues contact the device coordinator and/or Medical Control for guidance. Automated Implantable Cardioverter Defibrillator (AICD) / Pacemaker
If the patient reports a shock was delivered, assess cardiac rhythm. Follow standard protocols.
Do not remove the vest unless impeding necessary assessment or care. If removed, monitor cardiac rhythm. If a shock is delivered, assess patient and cardiac rhythm.
If blood glucose is < 60 mg/dL, ensure the pump is turned completely off or removed.
Do not disconnect or discontinue the pump. Note the medication and dose being infused, then contact Medical Control for guidance.
Access only if emergently needed and alternate IV access cannot be obtained (2 attempts). Central Venous Catheter / Tunneled Catheter / Medication Port
Do not access. Follow Intraosseous Access procedure if peripheral access cannot be obtained.
Prepare the medication to be administered. Refer to protocol specific indications and scope of practice for individual medications. Refer to Pharmacology section for drug specific information.

CROSS CHECK with another qualified provider that the correct medication is being administered to the correct patient via an appropriate route at an appropriate dose and that the medication is not expired.
Obtain IV access. Verify patency of the IV access site prior to administering any medication.

Administer the medication at the appropriate rate: • IV push: Rapid administration. • IV slow push: At least 30 seconds. Preferably 1 - 2 minutes. • Over X minutes: Slowly inject over the specified time frame. • Continuous infusion: Establish a drip at an appropriate dose / rate. • Via IV pump only: Establish a continuous infusion utilizing an IV pump.
Periodically reassess the administration site for signs of local reaction and/or infiltration of the IV. Immediately stop any infusion if the IV is no longer patent or becomes infiltrated.
Obtain IO access. Refer to Intraosseous Access procedure.
Follow steps above for IV medication administration.
Attach a syringe containing the full dose of the medication to be administered to the mucosal atomizing device (MAD).
Insert the MAD into one nostril, orienting the tip posteriorly. Administer half of the dose. Administer the other half of the dose in the second nostril. Do not exceed 1 mL per nostril.
Locate and expose an appropriate administration site (Deltoid or anterolateral thigh). Cleanse the site with an alcohol pad or disinfectant swab. Avoid any area of injury or infection.
Attach an appropriately sized needle to a syringe containing the dose of medication to be administered. Hold vertically (needle tip up) and depress the plunger to expel any air in the syringe.
Insert the needle perpendicular to the skin to the depth of the targeted muscle. Depress the plunger slowly, ensuring the full intended dose is administered, then withdraw and dispose of the needle.
Estimate insertion length by superimposing the tube over the body and measuring from nose to ear to xiphoid process. Note the length.
Lubricate the distal end of the tube with Lidocaine gel and pass it through the patient’s nostril posteriorly along the floor of the nasal passage. Do not orient the tip upward.
Continue to advance the tube gently until the measured length is reached. Ensure the tube is not coiled in the oropharynx.
Confirm placement: Inject 20 cc of air using a Toomey syringe while auscultating over the epigastrium for bubbles.
Secure the tube to the nose with tape and attach the proximal end of the tube to low/medium suction.
Document the indication, depth of insertion, and volume of any output.
Follow General-Universal Patient Care/Initial Patient Contact protocol.

Post delivery  Warm and maintain normal temperature.  Position / open airway (in a sniffing position – ear to sternal notch)  Dry and stimulate the newborn vigorously.  Clear secretions only if needed. Note: Routine suctioning is no longer recommended. ONLY perform tracheal suctioning if thick meconium present or if the airway is obstructed. If Labored Breathing or Persistent Cyanosis, in addition to above:
Give supplemental oxygen, as required.
Apply SpO monitor.

2 Assess blood glucose. If < 40 mg/dL during the first 72 hours of life or < 60mg/dL thereafter, administer: Dextrose 10% (D10W) 5 mL/kg IV/IO Repeat dose in 5 minutes, as needed. If Apneic/Gasping and/or HR is less below 100/min, in addition to above:
Begin positive pressure ventilation with BVM and 21% oxygen for 30 seconds, then increase to 100% oxygen. Ensure adequate chest rise. 40-60 breaths per minute.
Place supraglottic airway if necessary. Apply ETCO2 monitoring.
Apply ECG monitoring.
Intubate if unable to ventilate adequately by less invasive means If HR below 60/min or pulseless, in addition to above:
Begin chest compressions. Coordinate with ventilation. 3 compressions for each breath. 30 breaths per minute with chest compressions.
Obtain IV/IO access if not already obtained.
Administer: 0.9% Normal Saline 10 mL/kg IV/IO over 5 minutes Repeat as necessary, up to 30 mL/kg.
Administer: Epinephrine (Adrenaline) 0.01mg/kg (0.1mg/mL) IV/IO Repeat dose every 3-5 minutes until heart rate is > 60/min and palpable.
Assess for tension pneumothorax. Refer to Chest Decompression procedure.
Follow General – Universal Patient Care / Initial Patient Contact protocol.
Determine DNR status. Refer to Death & Criteria for Withholding Resuscitation protocol.

Begin chest compressions. Push hard and fast. Allow full chest recoil. Limit pauses to < 10 sec. Depth: 1/3 AP diameter of the chest or 1.5- 2” Rate: 100 – 120 bpm. Infant / Neonate : Use 2 fingers or thumbs Child: Use 1 hand
Administer 100% oxygen. Do not over-ventilate. Maintain compression-ventilation ratio 15:2 until advanced airway is established, then administer one breath every 2-3 seconds.

Apply AED / Assess cardiac rhythm every 2 minutes. If AED is advising to shock or rhythm is VF or VT (as determined by EMT-I or P), defibrillate at 2 J/kg then refer to Cardiac Arrest: Ventricular Fibrillation / Pulseless Ventricular Tachycardia protocol. If AED is advising no shock or rhythm is asystole or PEA (as determined by EMT-I or P), continue CPR then refer to Cardiac Arrest: Asystole / Pulseless Electrical Activity protocol.
Alternate compressors every 2 minutes or sooner if fatigued. If ETCO2 < 10 or dropping, reassess and optimize compression rate, depth, and recoil.
If ROSC is achieved, refer to Post Cardiac Arrest Care (ROSC) protocol.
If ROSC is not achieved, refer to Death and Criteria for Withholding Resuscitation protocol. Note: Once initiated, termination of resuscitative efforts is a Medical Control decision only.

Maintain a patent airway while manually stabilizing the cervical spine until an appropriately sized cervical collar or alternative is applied. Maintain alignment of the head, neck, and torso at all times.
Perform a focused neurologic assessment including GCS, motor, and sensory function.
Assess distal perfusion.
If necessary to lift/carry/maneuver the patient, utilize a long backboard, scoop stretcher, or extrication device with straps when feasible. Minimize flexion, extension, and rotation of the spine.

Once on the stretcher, the backboard, scoop stretcher, or extrication device may be removed. Consider leaving the patient on a long backboard to reduce the number of necessary movements if suspicion for injury is high or transport time is short.

SMR cannot be properly achieved with the patient in a sitting position. If elevation of the head is required, the device used to stabilize the spine should be elevated at the head while maintaining alignment of the neck and torso.
Contact Medical Control for guidance if the need for SMR is unclear.
Position the patient supine, expose, and cleanse the anterior neck. Use the non-dominant hand to identify and stabilize the thyroid cartilage and use the index finger to palpate the cricothyroid
membrane. Make a vertical incision (2 – 3 cm) across the cricothyroid membrane. Make a horizontal incision through the cricothyroid membrane (1 – 2 cm) and place the non-
dominant index finger into the airway.
Pass an endotracheal tube introducer / bougie into the trachea and withdraw the index finger.
Pass an endotracheal tube (size 4-0 to 6-0) over the bougie and withdraw the bougie.

Ventilate the patient and confirm / monitor placement with continuous ETCO2 box-waveform and SpO2. Ensure presence of bilateral breath sounds and secure the tube. Consider continuous manual stabilization.
Contact Medical Control and transport to the closest Emergency Department if airway cannot be secured.

Position the patient supine, expose and cleanse the anterior neck. Use the non-dominant hand to identify and stabilize the thyroid cartilage and use the index finger to palpate the cricothyroid membrane.

Attach a syringe filled with 0.9% Sodium Chloride onto a 14-guage catheter-needle. While aspirating the syringe, insert the needle at a 45-degree angle inferiorly through the cricothyroid membrane. When the trachea is entered, air will be aspirated easily. Do not advance the needle any further.
Advance the catheter over the needle, then withdraw the needle. Do not bend/kink the catheter.
Attach an adapter to the catheter and connect to an oxygen source. *

Ventilate the patient and confirm / monitor placement with continuous ETCO2 box-waveform and SpO2. Ensure presence of bilateral breath sounds. Maintain continuous manual stabilization of the catheter.
Contact Medical Control and transport to the closest Emergency Department.
Coordinate with law enforcement to ensure the weapon and patient are rendered safe to proceed. Refer to Behavioral Emergencies protocol and Patient Restraint policy, as needed.
Ensure the Taser cartridge is removed from the weapon or wires are cut prior to removing the darts.
Assess for injuries associated with burns, electrocution, and/or blunt trauma. Consider 12-Lead ECG.
Locate and expose both darts. If the darts have penetrated the eye, face, neck, breast, axilla, genitals, hands, or feet, leave them in place and transport to an Emergency Department for

removal. Use one hand to hold the skin around the barb taut. With the other hand, use a hemostat or forceps to grasp the electrode shaft. Pull straight out with a gentle, quick motion. Ensure the barb is intact.
Safely dispose of the dart in an appropriate container for sharp biohazards.
Provide wound care, as necessary. Apply a bandage over the wound sites.
If the barb cannot be safely, easily, and completely removed, transport to an Emergency Department for removal.
Completely expose the injury and assess for additional injuries.
Position the tourniquet proximal to the injury. Do not place across a joint or open fracture.
Tighten the tourniquet until bleeding stops and distal pulses are absent.
If bleeding is not controlled, apply a second tourniquet proximal and adjacent to the first.
Clearly indicate the time and date of application. Ensure the tourniquet remains exposed and visible.
Once applied, do not remove or loosen the tourniquet(s). Additional tightening may be required.
Consider pain control. Refer to Pain Control protocol.
If hemorrhage cannot be controlled, transport immediately to the nearest emergency department and contact Medical Control for guidance.
Remove any clothing covering the chest. Dry and/or shave the area, if necessary. Apply 4-Lead ECG and confirm rhythm.
Apply multi-function pads in anterior/posterior position and set cardiac monitor to pacing mode.
Set pacing rate at 80 beats per minute. Set initial current output to 50 mA. Confirm pacer “spikes” appear on cardiac monitor.
Slowly increase the pacer output (10 mA / 10 seconds) until electrical capture is achieved. Confirm mechanical capture by palpating femoral pulses. Reassess the patient.
If mechanical capture is not achieved despite maximum electrical output, discontinue pacing. Refer to Symptomatic Bradycardia protocol and contact Medical Control for guidance.
